method: similarity criteria on the listed facts: AA (two equal angle pairs), SSS (three equal side ratios), SAS (two equal side ratios with the included angle equal); otherwise "Not shown". Cross-check: whether the facts nevertheless determine the shape (SSA with the opposite side not shorter than the adjacent side) is recorded in the item note
assumptions: "Not shown to be similar" is read as "the listed facts do not establish similarity by AA / SSS / SAS".

ambiguous.prompt: In ΔABC and ΔPQR (A matches P, B matches Q, C matches R): AB = 2 cm, PQ = 4 cm; BC = 3 cm, QR = 6 cm; ∠A = ∠P = 40°. Which statement is true?
ambiguous.detail: two sides in proportion and an equal NON-included angle (SSA) with the opposite side not shorter than the adjacent side: the triangle is uniquely determined, so ABC and PQR are in fact similar (law of sines gives a second equal angle, then AA); "Not shown to be similar" is true only in the sense "not by AA/SSS/SAS", while the data do show similarity
